- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5% to avoid missing downside.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap 3–5 day highs at 10–15% below forecasted peak.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting downward; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to downward revisions.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 1.0 → 0.0 → 1.0), model overfits short-term momentum; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 80% of forecast, apply a “floor” correction to prevent underestimation bias.
